talk_enabled.description: Enable the talk service (UDP port 517). Provides real-time two-way chat using the original BSD talk protocol.

ntalk_enabled.description: Enable the ntalk service (UDP port 518). Preferred over talk for modern clients; offers better compatibility and ring notifications.

talk_user.description: Unix user account under which in.talkd runs. Root is typically required to write to system utmp and access privileged ports.

talkd_path.description: Absolute path to the in.talkd binary provided by the inetutils-talkd package.

extra_services.description: Additional services managed by inetd on this host beyond talk and ntalk. Each entry appends one inetd.conf line.

name.description: Service name matching an entry in /etc/services (e.g. 'ftp', 'telnet', 'time').

socket_type.description: Socket type: 'stream' for connection-oriented (TCP) or 'dgram' for datagram-based (UDP) services.

wait.description: Concurrency mode: 'wait' (inetd waits for server to exit; required for dgram) or 'nowait' (inetd forks per connection; typical for stream).

user.description: Unix user, optionally user.group, to run the server process as.

server_path.description: Absolute path to the server executable.

server_args.description: Space-separated argument list; first token is conventionally argv[0], usually the program's basename.

description.description: Short human-readable description of the service, emitted as a # comment line above the entry.

enabled.description: When false, the line is prefixed with # so the service is inactive without removing the entry.
